title: Our Cat Brings Home WARM Shoes 🐈
premise: Every night our ginger cat Biscuit carries a pair of old shoes in through the cat flap, always size eleven, always still warm, and nobody in town ever comes for them. Dad lines them up on the porch rail and says the cat goes on Saturday, and all week someone far too tall has walked one streetlight behind him on his way home from the bus.
twist: The tall stranger behind Dad is Biscuit himself, standing up in old shoes to walk Dad home, and at our gate he gets small again and climbs out of the boots. The shoes were never stolen, and a pair kept inside means somebody walks home alone.
world: a mint-green house with a white porch rail full of old shoes, a chalk count on a slate post, a picket gate, one long road of eight streetlights to a bus shelter, and a field of gold grass at sundown
